cards.explanation: The answer is in darkness. Isaiah says, “In darkness they do their works…” The whole plan is to hide where nobody can look. It's like sneaking a cookie off the cooling rack with the lights off, then standing there with crumbs on your shirt like it's a secret. Isaiah opens that line with “Woe.”

The answer is True. They say, “Who sees us, and who will know?” They're acting like the dark makes them invisible. It's like thinking nobody can hear you chewing a cookie because you turned the TV up. Isaiah answers that kind of thinking with “Woe.”

The answer is clay! Isaiah says it's turned upside down “…as if the potter were regarded as clay.” The one doing the shaping gets treated like the lump on the wheel. That's like a cookie turning to me and saying, "I stamped you." It's backwards, friends, and Isaiah says so.
The answer is False. Isaiah says, “In a very short time, will not Lebanon become an orchard, and the orchard seem like a forest?” Very short time. Nobody's checking a calendar for this one.

The words are hear and see. Isaiah says, “…the deaf will hear the words of the scroll…” A scroll is a written document, and words that were silent on it get heard. Then the verse says, “…out of the deep darkness the eyes of the blind will see.” Out of the deep darkness, friends, I picture a door opening and light coming in.

The answer is that they rejoice in God. Isaiah says, “The humble will increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.” Notice the word increase. Their joy goes up.
The answer is evil. Isaiah says “…all who look for evil will be cut down…” These are people who go searching for it. I think this one is heavy, friends.

The answer is with false charges. Isaiah says they are the ones “…who with false charges deprive the innocent of justice.” A charge that isn't true, used to take what an innocent person is owed. I think this one hurts, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “No longer will Jacob be ashamed and no more will his face grow pale.” No longer and no more, which is two ways of saying it's done. That's good news for the house of Jacob.
The answer is the work of My hands. When Jacob sees his children around him, the LORD calls them “…the work of My hands…” Hands are what a maker uses.

The answer is honor! The LORD says, “…they will honor My name, they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and they will stand in awe of the God of Israel.” That's three things in a row. That's what He says about Jacob's children once Jacob sees them around him.
The answer is True! The last line says, “…those who grumble will accept instruction.” The grumblers come around. In the same line, the wayward in spirit come to understanding.
